title: Node init-lock heuristics and cordon/drain scratchpad
content:
Context / symptom:
- Intermittent node join failures during scale-up (spot and on-demand) observed in prod clusters over last 2 weeks. Symptoms: node appears in cloud provider, cloud-init completes, but Kubernetes node stays NotReady or Ready then quickly NotReady. Some nodes get cordoned automatically by higher-level controller (k8s autoscaler integration) and never accept pods.

Why this doc:
- Quick scratchpad to capture commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses and temporary mitigations. Not a formal RCA yet. Mostly notes to self while iterating.

Commands run (chronological):
- Check node status and events:
  $ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep ip-10-
  $ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-32-45
    Events: NodeNotReady -> kubelet reports "Kubelet has not registered" (see below).

- Inspect kubelet logs on node (via ssh):
  $ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
  Recent chunks:
    Aug 31 09:14:12 kubelet[1234]: E0831 09:14:12.123456    1234 server.go:276] failed to run kubelet: could not init cloud provider: timed out waiting for the condition
    Aug 31 09:14:13 kubelet[1234]: error starting node lease controller: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to set up pod sandbox: failed to create containerd task: failed to create shim: "OCI runtime create failed: runc create failed: unable to start container process: error during container init: error creating device nodes: no such file or directory"

- Check container runtime and mounts:
  $ sudo systemctl status containerd
  $ sudo crictl ps -a || sudo docker ps -a
  $ ls -la /var/lib/containerd /var/lib/kubelet
  Observed that /var/lib/kubelet is a symlink to a block device mount that sometimes arrives late (cloud-init and attached volume race).

- cloud-init / cloud provider logs:
  $ sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init.log | grep -i kubelet
  cloud-init shows kubeadm join ran before the ephemeral disk was mounted in ~30% of failures. cloud-init unit ordering seemed fishy.

- Helm / daemonset interactions seen:
  - cluster-autoscaler cordon/uncordon webhook may cordon nodes preemptively if node doesn't report Ready within Xs. This hides the symptom (node cordoned) but root cause is kubelet/init ordering.

Error snippets collected:
- "could not init cloud provider: timed out waiting for the condition"
- "kubelet has not registered with master"
- "failed to create pod sandbox: error creating device nodes: no such file or directory"
- systemd: "A start job is running for Mount /var/lib/kubelet" (takes 2-10s, sometimes >30s)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Mount/disk attachment race: kubeadm/kubelet starts before device mount, creating missing directories or creating /var/lib/kubelet as regular dir; when later mount overlays a different fs, some files are lost or pids mismatch -> kubelet errors.
2) Kubelet TLS/CSR race: kubelet requests cert then tries to register before cloud provider identity available; cloud provider plugin returns transient error -> node remains NotReady.
3) Component ordering (systemd unit dependencies, cloud-init stages) are not strict in our AMI/packer template; certain kernels / initrd timing cause delayed udev/device creation.
4) Helm/Controllers: autoscaler/daemonset cordon triggers too aggressively on NotReady and don't retry uncordon after node recovers.

Quick experiments and outcomes:
- Experiment A: Add ExecStartPre sleep to kubelet.service on a test AMI (5s and 15s).
  - 5s: reduced failures marginally.
  - 15s: further reduction but increases join time. Not ideal.

- Experiment B: Change kubelet systemd unit to include After=var-lib-kubelet.mount and RequiresMountsFor=/var/lib/kubelet.
  - Result: much better in lab: mount ordering enforced, failures dropped. Needs bake.

- Experiment C: Modify cloud-init to run kubeadm join in a once-available hook (wait for mount and containerd socket). Patching cloud-init user-data to include:
    - systemd-run --on-active=1s --unit=wait-for-mount --description="wait for varlib" -- bash -c 'for i in {1..30}; do mountpoint -q /var/lib/kubelet && exit 0 || sleep 1; done; exit 1'
  - Result: Good for bootstrap; still seeing rare race on containerd socket.

- Experiment D: Tweak autoscaler to delay cordon to 60s (was 10s).
  - Result: fewer nodes stuck cordoned; but longer time before we reclaim capacity on bad nodes. Tradeoff.

Debugging snippets (useful commands to reproduce/check):
- Validate mount overlay issue:
  $ ls -ld /var/lib/kubelet /var/lib/kubelet/* || true
  $ stat /var/lib/kubelet
  $ findmnt /var/lib/kubelet || echo 'no mount'

- See if kubelet created files before mount (bad):
  $ sudo docker run --rm -v /var/lib/kubelet:/tmp/host ls -la /tmp/host || true

- Kubelet flags of interest (check via systemd):
  $ ps -ef | grep kubelet | grep -v grep
  Look for --root-dir, --pod-infra-container-image, --cloud-provider, --provider-id flags.

- Check CSR flow and certs:
  $ kubectl get csr | grep Pending
  $ sudo cat /var/lib/kubelet/pki/kubelet-client-current.pem || true

- Node lease/heartbeats:
  $ kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/ip-10-0-32-45/status" | jq '.status.conditions'

Temporary mitigations in prod (applied to most clusters):
- Bake change to kubelet systemd unit (RequiresMountsFor=/var/lib/kubelet) in AMI. Rolling out to one AZ canary.
- Increase autoscaler cordon delay to 60s to avoid permanent cordon on transient NotReady.
- Add a small cloud-init check to wait for containerd socket at /run/containerd/containerd.sock before starting kubeadm join.

Longer-term fixes to evaluate:
- Rework AMI to ensure mounts (ephemeral and persistent) are mounted earlier in boot (initramfs hooks).
- Move to explicit systemd mount units for ephemeral volumes so Depends/After can be used reliably.
- Add a light node-init daemon (systemd) that gates kubelet/kubeadm start until required resources (mounts, container runtime) are present; this is more robust than fixed sleeps.
- Improve controllers' heuristics (autoscaler, agent) to retry uncordon and to use node condition history rather than instant cordon.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need logs from a failed node with full journalctl (rotation may have removed earlier logs) — get one within 10 minutes of failure.
- Can we reproduce by artificially delaying mount in VM image test? (Plan: Packer run that inserts a sleep in udev/udevd unit).
- Is this correlated with certain kernel/hypervisor versions? Gather metadata: kernel version, hypervisor (GCE/AWS Nitro), instance type.
- Check if some clusters use kubeadm join with --cri-socket unset (defaults) while container runtime is containerd in others (explicit) — inconsistency may surface race.

Notes to self:
- If you hit a node that is cordoned but later becomes Ready, remember to uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>. But check why it was cordoned first.
- For reproductions, instrument cloud-init to dump /var/log/cloud-init-output.log and /var/log/cloud-init.log to GCS for each bootstrap attempt (auto-upload).

References:
- Past ticket: INFRA-4821 (attached) has older notes about ephemeral mount timing.
- kubelet systemd unit examples: refer to upstream kubeadm templates and our internal AMI repo (ami-configs/kubelet.service).

Quick checklist for next run (canary):
- [ ] Build test AMI with RequiresMountsFor=/var/lib/kubelet
- [ ] Update cloud-init join hook to wait for containerd socket
- [ ] Deploy canary in non-critical cluster (1 AZ)
- [ ] Monitor node join times and cordon counts for 6h window

End of scratchpad.

Other random obs:
- Saw one node where /etc/hosts had incorrect hostname (cloud-init wrote wrong FQDN) and kubelet refused registration until provider-id matched. Check cloud-init userdata variable substitution.

If I get distracted: search this file for 'mountpoint -q /var/lib/kubelet' to find the recommended quick gating snippet.
